title: Text about free $1,000 Walmart gift card is a fake
description: An old scam is making the rounds again in the Triad.

asr.full_text: I got this text out of the blue saying, congrats Ben, your code printed on your last receipt is among seven we randomly picked for a $1,000 Walmart gift card promotion. Woo hoo! We all want a thousand bucks, right? For free? Clearly, it sounds too good to be true. So instead of clicking that link right there, I Googled it first. Do this with any strange text or call you ever get. If it's a scam, someone's probably already posted about it first. Do this with any strange text or call you ever get. If it's a scam, someone's probably already posted about it online. When you Google put that message in quotation marks that helps you find it faster. In this case it turned out to be an old scam from 2012. The CBS station in Denver did do an old story about how Walmart does give away $1000 gift cards for completing surveys online, but they would never text you to say you won. They would send it in a certified letter. Turns out, clicking on that link could infect your phone with the virus or take you to a site where they try to get your personal information to steal your identity. So remember, anytime something looks too good to be true. Google it first.
